page_title: How To Create a Telegram Bot Using Python

summary.title: How To Create a Telegram Bot Using Python
summary.one_liner: You learn how to create a Telegram bot with BotFather, poll or receive updates through the Telegram API using the telepot library, and handle commands in a Django view that returns Planet Python RSS items.
keywords: how to make a telegram bot in python
takeaways: Create a bot by messaging BotFather, using /newbot, and choosing a username that ends in 'bot'.
Telegram offers two mutually exclusive update methods: polling with getUpdates or receiving pushes through a webhook set with setWebhook, which requires HTTPS.
Use telepot to call getMe, getUpdates and sendMessage, and use update_id offsets to read only new messages.
Build a Django view that receives POST updates, dispatches commands like /start, help and feed, and replies with sendMessage.
Test the webhook locally by sending a saved Update JSON body to the view with Postman before deploying.
summary.summary: The article walks through creating a Telegram bot named PlanetPythonBot via BotFather and explains the two API update approaches: getUpdates polling and webhooks. It uses the telepot library to make getMe, getUpdates and sendMessage calls. The author then builds a Django view that parses the Planet Python RSS feed with requests and handles commands such as /start, help and feed. The bot is tested locally by sending a POST request with Postman. Deployment and SSL setup for the webhook are deferred to Part 2, which is not included on this page. The code is written for Python 2 (print statement, cElementTree).
